title: Microsoft Purview Insider Risk Management: priority content for the Risky AI usage template
summary: The briefing passes: the roadmap targets, policy settings, permissions and product licensing are supported. The priority-content path stops before the content-selection buttons, and three background statements need their supporting Microsoft references added.

claims.claim: Microsoft plans priority content support for the Risky AI usage policy template.
claims.quote: With this update, Risky AI usage policy template will support priority content.

claims.claim: Customers can define sensitive info types as priority content.
claims.quote: Customers can define Sensitive Info Types (SITs), Trainable Classifiers, Sensitivity Labels as priority content

claims.claim: Customers can define trainable classifiers as priority content.
claims.quote: Customers can define Sensitive Info Types (SITs), Trainable Classifiers, Sensitivity Labels as priority content

claims.claim: Customers can define sensitivity labels as priority content.
claims.quote: Customers can define Sensitive Info Types (SITs), Trainable Classifiers, Sensitivity Labels as priority content

claims.claim: The planned support permits alerts only when activity matches selected priority content.
claims.quote: and get alerted only when the activity matches the selected priority content.

claims.claim: This roadmap item concerns Microsoft Purview Insider Risk Management.
claims.quote: "title": "Microsoft Purview: Insider Risk Management-Priority content support for Risky AI usage"

claims.claim: The roadmap record was modified on 2026-10-12T23:01:05.
Learn already lists Risky AI usage among templates supporting priority content.
claims.quote: The following policy templates support priority content selection: ... Risky AI usage

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Specifying priority content increases risk scores for associated activity.
claims.quote: Specifying content as a priority increases the risk score for any associated activity

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; Governance guidance
claims.claim: Prioritising content increases the chance of a high severity alert.
claims.quote: which in turn increases the chance of generating a high severity alert.

claims.claim: A policy can assign risk scores and generate alerts only for specified activities containing priority content.
claims.quote: The Scoring detail page allows you to scope the policy to only assign risk scores and generate alerts for specified activities that include priority content.

claims.where: Why it matters; Risk assessment: Security & identity; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Activities without priority content are not scored under priority-only scoring, subject to the stated cumulative-exfiltration exception.
claims.quote: Activities without priority content aren't scored ... Cumulative exfiltration activity always receives a risk score, regardless of whether or not it contains prioritized content.

claims.where: Why it matters; Governance guidance: After rollout
claims.claim: Unscored activities can still be reviewed if an alert is generated.
claims.quote: Activities without priority content aren't scored, but you can still review them if an alert is generated.

claims.claim: Cumulative exfiltration activity is always scored regardless of priority content.
claims.quote: The option to only score activities containing priority content doesn't apply to cumulative exfiltration activities. Cumulative exfiltration activity always receives a risk score

claims.claim: Some activities generate no alert unless content contains a built-in or custom SIT or is prioritised in the policy.
claims.quote: some activities don't generate an alert at all unless the related content contains built-in or custom sensitive info types or you specify it as a priority in the policy.

claims.claim: Configuring priority-only alerts does not change risk score boosters.
claims.quote: If you configure a policy to generate alerts only for activity that includes priority content, no changes are applied to risk score boosters.

claims.claim: Risky AI usage detects user browsing to generative AI websites.
claims.quote: Detection focuses on user browsing activities to generative AI websites

claims.claim: Risky AI usage detects sensitive user prompts in Microsoft 365 Copilot, Microsoft Copilot and agents.
claims.quote: user prompts and AI responses containing sensitive information in Microsoft 365 Copilot, Microsoft Copilot, and agents.

claims.claim: Risky AI usage detects sensitive AI responses in Microsoft 365 Copilot, Microsoft Copilot and agents.
claims.quote: user prompts and AI responses containing sensitive information in Microsoft 365 Copilot, Microsoft Copilot, and agents.

claims.claim: Risky activity detected by this policy contributes to Adaptive Protection user risk scoring.
claims.quote: Detection of risky activity by this policy also contributes to the user risk scoring in Adaptive Protection.

claims.quote: When using this template, you must configure the Microsoft Insider risk extension (on Microsoft Edge browser) or Microsoft Purview extension (on Chrome browser) on the user devices.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Change & support; Scope; Cost and licensing

claims.quote: Risky AI usage ... At least one browsing indicator selected in the policy

claims.claim: Insider Risk Management supports up to 100 policies for each template.
claims.quote: Insider Risk Management supports up to 100 policies for each policy template.

claims.claim: A policy can select up to five trainable classifiers.
claims.quote: Users configuring a policy that selects Trainable classifiers in the policy workflow can select up to 5 trainable classifiers to apply to the policy.

claims.quote: | Actions | Insider Risk Management | Insider Risk Management Admins | ... | Configure policies and settings | Yes | Yes |

claims.quote: | Actions | Insider Risk Management | Insider Risk Management Admins | Insider Risk Management Analysts | ... | Access & investigate alerts | Yes | No | Yes |

claims.claim: Administrative units scope restricted administrators when they configure policies.
claims.quote: Scoped in the following table means that the admin actions for that role are limited by their assigned admin unit. ... | Configure policies | Scoped | Scoped |

claims.claim: The priority-content route is Microsoft Purview portal > Insider Risk Management > Policies > Create policy > Policy template > policy category > Risky AI usage > Content to prioritize > I want to prioritize content.
claims.quote: On the Policy template page, choose a policy category and then select the template for the new policy. ... On the Content to prioritize page ... I want to prioritize content
claims.fix: Keep the route, which reaches the priority-content option. Append to controls[0].note: 'On the subsequent detail pages, select Sensitive info type > Add sensitive info type, Sensitivity labels > Add sensitivity label, or Trainable classifiers > Add trainable classifier to choose the content.' These last steps are documented at https://learn.microsoft.com/purview/insider-risk-management-configure; the Risky AI usage template's applicability is documented at the already-cited https://learn.microsoft.com/purview/insider-risk-management-policies.

claims.claim: No documented PowerShell, Graph or other API configures this policy's priority-content selection.
claims.quote: Searched: Insider Risk Management priority content PowerShell; Insider Risk Management priority content Graph API scoring. Read configure, policies and search excerpts on Defender IRM Graph integration; no operation sets priority content.

claims.claim: Priority-only alerts are set through Microsoft Purview portal > Insider Risk Management > Policies > Create policy > Policy template > policy category > Risky AI usage > Content to prioritize > I want to prioritize content > Scoring > Get alerts only for activity that includes priority content.
claims.quote: If you select I want to prioritize content ... Scoring: Decide whether to assign risk scores to all risk management activities detected by this policy or only for activities that include priority content. Choose Get alerts for all activity or Get alerts only for activity that includes priority content.

claims.claim: No documented PowerShell, Graph or other API sets priority-only scoring and alerts.
claims.quote: Searched: Insider Risk Management priority content PowerShell; Insider Risk Management priority content Graph API scoring. Read configure, policies and Defender IRM Graph integration search excerpts; documented Graph operations concern alerts, not policy scoring settings.

claims.claim: Role-group membership is configured in Microsoft Purview portal > Settings > Roles and groups > Roles groups > Insider Risk Management > Edit > Choose users.
claims.quote: Select Settings ... select Roles and groups, then select Roles groups ... Select the Insider Risk Management role group, then select Edit. ... Select Choose users

claims.claim: Add-RoleGroupMember -Identity "<role-group>" -Member "<user-UPN>" adds a user to a role group using parameters available in Security & Compliance PowerShell.
claims.quote: Use the Add-RoleGroupMember cmdlet to add members to a management role group. ... -Identity ... Security & Compliance ... -Member ... Security & Compliance ... User ID or user principal name (UPN)

claims.claim: The general workflow has detail pages for selecting SITs, labels and trainable classifiers, and lists additional priority types.
claims.quote: Use these detail pages to define the SharePoint, sensitive info types, sensitivity labels, trainable classifiers, and file extensions to prioritize in the policy.

claims.claim: The configure page does not name the Risky AI usage template's policy category.
claims.quote: Searched: configure page text for Policy template and Risky AI usage; read Create policy steps. It says choose a policy category, then a template, but never names Risky AI usage or its category.

claims.claim: An existing policy is opened from Insider Risk Management > Policies and changed using Edit policy.
claims.quote: Select Policies in the left navigation. ... select the policy you want to update. ... On the policy details page, select Edit policy.

claims.claim: The template of an existing policy cannot be edited.
claims.quote: You can't edit the Policy template or Name field.

claims.claim: The name of an existing policy cannot be edited.
claims.quote: You can't edit the Policy template or Name field.

claims.where: front matter: defaultState; What's changing; Open questions; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Microsoft has not stated the priority-content change's default state on arrival.
claims.quote: Searched: Risky AI usage priority content default existing policies. Read roadmap, configure workflow, policies and template excerpts; no arrival default stated. The default for Risky Agents is a different template.

claims.claim: Microsoft has not stated that existing Risky AI usage policies change automatically on arrival.
claims.quote: Searched: Risky AI usage priority content default existing policies. Read roadmap, configure, policies and returned DSPM one-click policy excerpts; none describes automatic changes to existing policies from this update.

claims.where: What's changing; Scope; Governance guidance; Open questions
claims.claim: The policies page gives no cloud scope confirming its priority-content guidance for GCC, GCC High and DoD.
claims.quote: Searched: policies page text for cloud and GCC; Risky AI usage priority content GCC; Risky AI usage priority content GCC GCC High DoD. Read policies and government deployment search excerpts; no cloud-specific confirmation of this update found.

claims.claim: Learn describes no action on users performed by the priority-content setting itself.
claims.quote: Searched: Insider Risk Management priority content automatic actions users. Read policies, configure and Adaptive Protection search excerpts. Priority content sets scores and alerts; separate Adaptive Protection policies implement preventive actions.

claims.claim: The sources describe no end-user-visible experience introduced by this update.
claims.quote: Searched: Risky AI usage priority content default existing policies; priority content automatic actions users. Read roadmap, policies, configure and templates; the update is described as an administrator's scoring and alert configuration.

claims.where: controls[1].note; Risk assessment; Governance guidance: At rollout
claims.claim: Get alerts for all activity is the alternative that does not restrict policy scoring to priority-content matches.
claims.quote: Decide whether to assign risk scores to all risk management activities detected by this policy or only for activities that include priority content. Choose Get alerts for all activity or Get alerts only for activity that includes priority content.

claims.claim: The roadmap describes priority-content alert matching rather than describing new data collection.
claims.quote: With this update, Risky AI usage policy template will support priority content. Customers can define Sensitive Info Types (SITs), Trainable Classifiers, Sensitivity Labels as priority content, and get alerted only when the activity matches the selected priority content.

claims.claim: SIT definitions are managed elsewhere in Purview, outside this policy's priority-content selection.
claims.quote: Sign in to the Microsoft Purview portal > Information Protection > Classifiers > Sensitive info types and choose the sensitive information type from the list that you want to modify.
claims.fix: Add https://learn.microsoft.com/purview/sit-manage-custom-sits-compliance-center to sources to support the statement that SITs are managed elsewhere; no additional control row is needed.

claims.claim: Sensitivity labels themselves are managed elsewhere in Purview.
claims.quote: When you have published sensitivity labels from the Microsoft Purview portal, they start to appear in Office apps for users to classify and protect data as it's created or edited.
claims.fix: Add https://learn.microsoft.com/purview/sensitivity-labels-office-apps to sources to support the statement about labels being managed elsewhere; do not add a new control row.

claims.claim: Classifiers themselves are managed elsewhere in Purview.
claims.quote: The Classifiers page brings classification types together in one experience where you can discover, create, inspect, and manage classifiers. ... In the Microsoft Purview portal, you can access Classifiers under Information Protection, Data Loss Prevention, or DSPM
claims.fix: Add https://learn.microsoft.com/purview/data-classification-overview to sources to support the statement about classifiers being managed elsewhere; no additional control row is needed.
